text:
Preregister a narrow hypothesis: stronger baseline sensitivity to recent-history perturbations predicts larger gains from the fixed SASRec recency-loss variant. Freeze perturbations, diagnostic sign, aggregation, threshold, variant hyperparameters and analysis before examining intervention outcomes. A proposed decision rule: deploy the variant when diagnostic D exceeds fixed threshold τ; otherwise retain baseline. Train both models on all four categories to evaluate this rule against always-baseline and always-variant policies. Prespecification follows [PATH guidance](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7531587/); this recommender design is a proposed adaptation. Previously inspected outcomes cannot become prospective evidence through retrospective registration.

Separate controls by purpose. Use matched older-history perturbations, controlling deletion count and remaining sequence length, to probe recency specificity. Enumerate all 24 assignments of dataset diagnostics to observed gains; compare the preregistered association statistic and decision-rule value against this correspondence-breaking null. With an exchangeability assumption, this tests whether diagnostic matching carries information beyond overall intervention benefit. It does not establish mechanism; heterogeneous categories weaken exchangeability. Preserve paired user outcomes, consistent with [paired-permutation methods](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.01416).

For each identical validation user and candidate set, compute variant-minus-baseline hit@10, then average within category and equally across categories. Bootstrap paired users separately within categories for a macro-gain interval; this conditions on fixed training runs and candidates. Report category gains and discordant hit counts; [offline-evaluation research](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-020-09371-3) emphasizes user-level comparisons. Four dataset observations make association fragile: 24 permutations give minimum one-sided p=1/24; four-category sign flips give minimum conventional two-sided p=2/16. Users are not additional independent dataset-level observations. One variant can support this diagnostic–intervention pairing on these categories, not broad diagnostic usefulness, optimal intervention selection, causal mechanism, or generalization to new datasets.
